title: Migrate structured run config from config.md to schema-validated TOML
description:
Markdown is the wrong container for machine-parsed, fail-closed configuration. .tick/config.md currently carries four kinds of STRUCTURED data that a program parses and that fails closed on a mistake — Testing commands, Closeout Evidence Commands, Acceptance Evidence mappings, and the Pi Orchestrator key/value block — alongside genuine prose (Rules) that implementers read verbatim into a prompt.

The working rule this epic applies: if a PROGRAM parses it and a mistake fails closed, it needs a schema; if a MODEL reads it, markdown is right.

Evidence the current shape costs us: the Acceptance Evidence contract had to invent verbatim-and-uniquely-matching with fail-closed handling of duplicate, ambiguous, unknown, injected, missing and cross-item evidence. That entire apparatus exists only because markdown has no structure — a schema supplies uniqueness, typing and validation for free. The Pi Orchestrator block is worse: it is key/value config in markdown that DUPLICATES role and tier routing runners.toml already expresses with a JSON schema, so one change needs two edits.

Blast radius is contained: only extensions/ticks-runner/config.ts (298 lines) parses these sections; no Go code does — internal/herd/config already reads runners.toml. So this is one TS module, its tests, the skill docs, and a migration path for existing repos.

Target: extend .tick/runners.toml (already the how-work-executes file, already the only tick config surface with a schema) rather than inventing a fourth config file. Rules and narrative testing hints stay in config.md.

Backward compatibility is mandatory — other repos have config.md today and must keep working.
notes: 2026-08-19 18:46 - Cross-epic interaction found by ko8 tick 3q2: cloud/sandbox/preflight.sh deliberately mirrors the single-inline-code-span parsing rule in extensions/ticks-runner/config.ts (parseExecutableCommands) — it is a cross-implementation parity point of the kind .tick/learnings.md warns about. This epic replaces that markdown parsing with schema-validated TOML, so the migration must either update preflight.sh to read the structured config too, or explicitly state that it keeps consuming the legacy markdown path and why. Do not let the two drift silently: a Phase 1 sandbox pre-flight reading a format the runner no longer writes fails at run time, in a container, with no terminal.
acceptance_criteria: A repo with only runners.toml runs an epic end to end with no config.md structured sections; a repo with only the legacy markdown still works and emits one deprecation warning naming the migration command; tk config migrate converts a real config.md, leaving prose behind, and the result validates against the schema; unknown keys fail closed rather than being ignored; this repo has migrated and its own runs are green; skill docs describe only the new shape with a documented legacy fallback.
